A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KOR-Bench and provide readable main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices. The original appendices A–F match v3 appendices C–H, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 60 models, plus cipher-step, self-correction, complex-task, puzzle-hint and attention analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds two o1 models, dataset-size analyses, benchmark correlations and experiments without explicit rules.

M1.justification: The benchmark's core procedures, original prompting strategies, self-correction, stepwise analysis and attention aggregation remain unchanged. The construction pipeline is newly documented, but the PDFs do not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: The five categories, 125 rules and 1,250 questions remain unchanged. Appendix K adds scenarios without explicit rules, including inferring rules from three examples, extending task requirements beyond applying supplied rules. Appendix J additionally analyzes aggregate scores from six other benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds o1-preview-2024-09-12 and o1-mini-2024-09-12 while retaining all 60 earlier model rows. The original diagnostic comparisons retain their model sets, making this a limited comparator expansion.

E3.justification: Appendices I–K introduce substantial new evaluation designs: sampling varying dataset fractions within rules or categories, correlating benchmark scores across 21 models, and testing 16 models without rules under zero-shot and three-shot conditions. The original main evaluation and scoring procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 retains the original diagnostic analyses and adds tests of dataset-size sensitivity, relationships with other benchmarks, and dependence on explicit rules. These address benchmark reliability and validity questions that v1 did not experimentally examine.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's token-length summaries, Appendix I newly reports means and standard deviations of accuracy discrepancies under subsampling, alongside score dispersion through the Gini coefficient. This adds descriptive variability reporting, without disclosing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 60 retained Table 2 model rows keep their numerical scores, but new o1 results of 72.88% and 70.16% change the overall leaders. Figures 13–14 and Tables 14–15 add substantial results; for example, GPT-4o scores 12.56% and 29.92% in the new zero-shot and three-shot rule-free conditions. These do not replace its original 58.00% result.

T1.justification: New Appendix A formalizes the previously verbal knowledge-orthogonality concept through knowledge–rule independence, conditional belief quantities, a knowledge-impact factor beta, rule-centrality conditions and an adjustment equation. This substantially expands the mathematical definition of the central construct, although no supporting theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion update the leading-model claim from Claude-3.5-Sonnet/GPT-4o to o1 and emphasize the benchmark's differentiation between models. The introduction also explicitly accommodates background knowledge assisting reasoning. The central five-category benchmark contribution and knowledge-decoupling aim remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets subset stability as benchmark robustness and benchmark correlations as support for reasoning-oriented validity. It explains rule-free failures through insufficient information and differences in how readily examples reveal rules, and adds discussion of nonmonotonic model-size effects. The original error-case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix B newly document human, code and LLM roles in rule design, question generation and iterative quality/difficulty filtering. This improves construction disclosure without establishing a changed pipeline. Existing prompt templates and extraction details remain, and the release statement still promises future dataset/code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds the OpenAI o1 reference and McKenzie et al.'s inverse-scaling work, linking the latter to Qwen2.5-32B outperforming 72B. The related-work taxonomy and most research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, conclusion and several analysis paragraphs are tightened or rewritten; Section 4's numbered subsections become labeled paragraphs, and future plans move into the reproducibility/ethics text. The overall narrative and extensive retained appendices remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a construction diagram, a six-panel dataset-size figure, a correlation heatmap and two rule-free results tables. The original task-example figure survives as Figure 3, while Table 2 expands and moves model-version identifiers into row labels. These substantially extend the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The construction documentation and new size-sensitivity and rule-omission analyses improve transparency and provide useful validation missing from v1. The gain is limited because correlations and rule dependence do not establish knowledge independence. The new formalization also leaves unresolved how beta approaching -1 fits its approximate-equality rule-centrality condition.
